title: Invalid Tweets
statement:
One table stores the posts of a social network:

- `Tweets(tweet_id, content)`: one row per tweet; `tweet_id` is unique. `content` contains only letters, digits, `!` and spaces.

A tweet is **invalid** when its `content` is longer than 15 characters (16 or more). Every character counts, spaces and `!` included; a tweet of exactly 15 characters is still valid.

Report the `tweet_id` of every invalid tweet, in a single column named `tweet_id`. Rows may come in any order.
constraints: content contains only letters, digits, "!" and spaces, at most 50 characters
brute:
SELECT t.tweet_id
FROM Tweets AS t
WHERE t.content LIKE '________________%'

Tweets: More than fifteen chars are here!
More than fifteen chars are here!

notes:
## Intuition

Validity depends on one row at a time: a tweet is reported exactly when its text has more than 15 characters. No joins or grouping are needed, only a length function inside a `WHERE` filter.

## Approach

1. Read every row of `Tweets`.
2. `CHAR_LENGTH(content)` counts the characters of the tweet, spaces and `!` included.
3. `WHERE ... > 15` keeps the tweets with 16 or more characters, and `SELECT tweet_id` reports their ids.

## Example 1, step by step

| tweet_id | content | `CHAR_LENGTH(content)` | `> 15`? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Let us Code | 11 | no |
| 2 | More than fifteen chars are here! | 33 | yes |

Only tweet 2 passes the filter, so the output is the single row `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(T · L) for T tweets of length at most L, one scan with a length computation per row.
- Space: O(T) for the result in the worst case.

## Pitfalls

- Using `>= 15` reports tweets of exactly 15 characters, which are valid.
- `LENGTH` counts bytes, not characters; it agrees here only because the content is plain ASCII, so `CHAR_LENGTH` states the intent better.
- Spaces count: a tweet of 16 spaces is invalid even though it has no visible text.

## Clauses

| Name | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Tweets` | the only table; each row is checked on its own |
| `CHAR_LENGTH(content)` | the number of characters in the tweet |
| `WHERE ... > 15` | keeps only the invalid tweets |

narration.1: Only the ids of the invalid tweets are reported.
narration.2: Every tweet is examined on its own, so the single table is all we need.
narration.3: CHAR_LENGTH counts every character, spaces and exclamation marks included, and more than 15 means invalid.
